text:
jules (arch): Quick idea — Endpoint Harmonizer: a lightweight request translation layer in front of runtime to accept v1/v2 payload shapes and normalise to canonical vNext. Keeps clients stable while we prune surfaces.
jules (arch): Goals: no client SDK changes for 6 months, observable translation metrics, per-tenant opt-in/opt-out, and a safe sunset path.
ana? matt thoughts on perf impact? :thinking:
matt (eng-runtime): Sounds sane. Main concern is extra hop + JSON transforms increasing p50 for short requests. We should microbenchmark.
matt (eng-runtime): If we colocate translator in the same pod/process as the runtime (inproc lib), latency is minimal but deployment coupling gets messy.
ana: Another angle — run it as an ingress sidecar (nginx-ish) so we can roll per-cluster and version independently.
riyaz (eng-infra): Sidecar makes ops easier but duplicates state/metrics and increases memory footprint across fleet. Sidecar also complicates tenant quotas if it's outside runtime.
jules (arch): Tradeoffs: inproc = lower latency, higher coupling. Sidecar = operational independence, higher infra cost. Gateway = single point of change, easier to test but scaling differences.
tanya (eng-ml): Also need model semantics mapping. v1 had "instructions", v2 uses "system_prompt" + structured steps. Harmonizer must offer semantics-preserving mapping where possible and emit regression telemetry when it can't.
jules (arch): UX for clients: header x-harmonizer-opt: "on|off" and feature flag per-tenant. Default on for 6 months then off by tenants who opt out.
matt (eng-runtime): Ops checklist suggestion:

1) implement translator as a library loaded by runtime (fast path)
2) expose translation logs and counters (mapped_count, dropped_fields, rewrite_latency_ms)
3) canary route for 1% traffic via translator, with continuous monitors

ana: + add a safety fallback to "legacy passthrough" when translation fails with 502 -> triggers alert and auto-rollback.
riyaz (eng-infra): We should prefix all translated requests with X-Original-Version and X-Translation-Id to trace back in logs. Also generate a synthetic UUID for correlation.
jules (arch): example mapping sketch:

```json
// client v1
{
  "instructions": "Summarize this",
  "context": "..."
}
// harmonizer output (vNext canonical)
{
  "system_prompt": "",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this"}
  ],
  "meta": {"orig_version": "v1"}
}
```
matt (eng-runtime): Nice. We should quantify token delta and KV cache cold-start impact — translations may expand tokens.
tanya (eng-ml): We'll create an eval harness to check quality drift on a thousand real prompts. If quality < 0.98 we hold.
ana: Rollout plan (ops-friendly):

- Phase 0: implement library + unit tests
- Phase 1: internal canary (dev org) 0.1% traffic, 1 week
- Phase 2: customer opt-in flag, 5% traffic, 2 weeks
- Phase 3: default-on for all non-enterprise, telemetry windows 1 month
- Phase 4: announce deprecation window and start graceful sunset

matt (eng-runtime): Telemetry to track:

- translation_rate (per-tenent)
- translation_latency_ms p50/p95
- field_drops
- quality_regressions (from tanya's evals)

riyaz (eng-infra): Cost estimate: sidecar approach adds ~300MB per pod. Inproc adds ~0.5ms median but no extra RAM. Need numbers before we pick.
jules (arch): Decision proposed: start with inproc translator library (fast), add a gateway mode later if ops ask for it. Use per-tenant flag and 3-month default-on window.
ana: +1 for gradual. Need runbook: kill switch route to disable translation cluster-wide (for incidents).
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: harmonizer-v0.1 -> arch-canary namespace at 1719010200. Logs: /deploys/harmonizer/1719010200
matt (eng-runtime): I'll draft a microbenchmark for translation overhead and post results here tomorrow.
tanya (eng-ml): I'll start the quality harness and share baseline metrics. Expect first report in 5 days.
jules (arch): OK, next steps: matt + tanya + riyaz to own POC. ana to draft opt-in flag spec and migration docs. We'll reconvene Fri.
ana: tagging @matt @tanya @riyaz — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
